prompt_en: A cinematic Stonepunk environmental portrait inside a tidal observatory carved from colossal concentric basalt rings. An unmistakably adult woman, using the supplied portrait only for facial appearance, has long near-black wavy hair, warm brown almond-shaped eyes, softly arched brows, a slim oval face, and natural rose lips. She wears a black woven-flax mantle armored with overlapping polished-shale plates and stone fasteners. At blue hour she locks a fist-sized quartz chronometer into a hand-cranked stone astrolabe. Her left hand braces the crystal socket while her right turns a carved granite crank. Interlocking basalt gears, counterweighted monolith arms, and grooved circular tracks visibly transmit the motion: one outer ring has shifted open toward a breaking wave. Veins of quartz embedded through the mechanism glow and trace measured tide lines across raised carvings. Salt spray catches the mineral light; wet stone, wind-tossed hair, and precise hand contact ground the scene as physically photographed working technology. Use a medium-wide three-quarter frame that keeps her face, both hands, the gear train, and opened sea aperture readable. Fitted ring joints, carved channels, and raised measurement marks stay sharp. A 40 mm lens at deep focus layers her, the mechanism, and the sea. Blue-hour skylight and quartz glow share reflections across skin, flax, shale, and wet basalt as the breaking wave throws spray through the aperture.
